title: Multi-omics Integration of Single-cell and Spatial Transcriptomics with Tissue and Urine Proteomics Identifies TRIM28 as a Translationally Relevant Candidate Regulator in Acute Kidney Injury.
authors: Wang, Kangyu; Wang, Hao; Zhang, Yalong; Zhang, Zijian; Xu, Changhong; Zhao, Hong; Ma, Jiaxuan; Man, Jiangwei; Yang, Li
one_liner_zh: 该研究整合多组学数据识别AKI候选调控因子TRIM28，虽涉及分子对接和MD模拟，但核心是疾病机制与生物标志物发现，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合体系，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) lacks disease-modifying therapies, partly because cell type-specific injury programs remain incompletely resolved and tissue mechanisms are not readily translated into clinically accessible biomarkers. We constructed a cross-scale, multi-omics atlas to prioritize candidate regulator linking renal injury circuitry with urine-detectable signals. Human single-cell, bulk, and spatial transcriptomics were integrated with mouse renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (RIRI) kidney proteomics and clinical urine proteomics. Overlap of differentially expressed genes and differentially abundant proteins nominated candidates, which were ranked by a random forest model. Immune remodeling was assessed by deconvolution and pathway enrichment, with spatial localization supported by reference-based deconvolution. Therapeutic tractability was explored by structure-based virtual screening, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA). TRIM28 was evaluated in HK-2 hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R) and mouse RIRI models using genetic perturbation, expression validation, and in vitro pharmacologic evaluation. Integration converged on five genes (TRIM28, HNRNPH1, ARHGEF10L, C1RL, and UCHL3), with TRIM28 showing the highest feature importance and links to inflammatory, immune, metabolic, and proliferative programs. AKI exhibited intensified intercellular communication and an innate-skewed immune landscape. TRIM28 was robustly upregulated in HK-2 H/R and mouse RIRI kidneys and was also directly detected in the human urine proteome. In HK-2 cells, TRIM28 knockdown dampened, whereas overexpression amplified, IL-17-linked inflammatory signaling and apoptotic responses. Docking-prioritized HY-N10592 improved viability, reduced H/R-associated TRIM28 induction, IL-17-linked output, and apoptotic marker activation, and showed CETSA-supported cellular engagement of TRIM28. This integrative framework prioritizes TRIM28 as a candidate regulator linking tubular injury mechanisms with clinically relevant urinary signals and nominates HY-N10592 as a candidate chemical tool with CETSA-supported cellular target engagement for further mechanistic and in vivo evaluation in AKI.
abstract_zh: 急性肾损伤（AKI）缺乏疾病修饰疗法，部分原因在于细胞类型特异性损伤程序尚未完全阐明，且组织机制难以直接转化为临床可获取的生物标志物。我们构建了一个跨尺度、多组学图谱，以优先筛选连接肾损伤回路与尿液可检测信号的候选调控因子。将人类单细胞、批量及空间转录组学与小鼠肾缺血再灌注损伤（RIRI）肾脏蛋白质组学及临床尿液蛋白质组学进行整合。差异表达基因与差异丰度蛋白的重叠筛选出候选因子，并通过随机森林模型进行排序。通过去卷积和通路富集评估免疫重塑，空间定位由基于参考的去卷积支持。治疗可行性通过基于结构的虚拟筛选、分子对接、分子动力学模拟和细胞热位移分析（CETSA）进行探索。在HK-2缺氧/复氧（H/R）和小鼠RIRI模型中，利用遗传扰动、表达验证和体外药理学评估对TRIM28进行评价。整合分析聚焦于五个基因（TRIM28、HNRNPH1、ARHGEF10L、C1RL和UCHL3），其中TRIM28显示出最高的特征重要性，并与炎症、免疫、代谢和增殖程序相关。AKI表现出增强的细胞间通讯和先天偏斜的免疫景观。TRIM28在HK-2 H/R和小鼠RIRI肾脏中显著上调，并直接在人类尿液蛋白质组中被检测到。在HK-2细胞中，TRIM28敲低减弱了IL-17相关炎症信号和凋亡反应，而过表达则增强这些反应。基于对接优先排序的HY-N10592提高了细胞活力，减少了H/R相关的TRIM28诱导、IL-17相关输出和凋亡标志物激活，并显示出CETSA支持的TRIM28细胞结合。该整合框架将TRIM28优先列为连接肾小管损伤机制与临床相关尿液信号的候选调控因子，并提名HY-N10592作为候选化学工具，其具有CETSA支持的细胞靶点结合，可用于AKI中进一步的机制和体内评估。
